item.title: Datasette Charts plugin updates improve hooks and adds documentation website
item.description:
Datasette Charts plugin updates improve hooks and adds documentation website

The datasette-charts plugin has released an update addressing friction points identified in its chart type plugin hooks, along with the launch of a dedicated documentation website.

🔍 Overview

The datasette-charts plugin features a hook system that allows other plugins to define new chart types. To test this functionality, Claude Opus 5.5 was used to build an experimental plugin, which revealed several friction points in the design. The current release addresses these issues to improve the development process for additional chart plugins.

⚙️ Key details

  • The release improves the ergonomics of building additional chart plugins.
  • Friction points identified by an experimental Claude Opus 5.5 plugin have been resolved.

🚀 Availability

  • A new website for the plugin is available at charts.datasette.io.
  • The website includes a tutorial for plugin authors.
  • A gallery displays core charts and annotations, with each item linking to an interactive demo on Datasette Lite.

#Datasette #Python #DataVisualization #Plugins #AIAssistedDevelopment

Source: Release: datasette-charts 0.4a0

item.title: Datasette Adds Chart Annotations for Enhanced Data Visualization
item.description:
Datasette Adds Chart Annotations for Enhanced Data Visualization

I added chart annotations to datasette-charts! You can now render a chart and then annotate it with lines, shaded areas, labels, or a combination of the three.

📊 What’s New

  • Add lines, shaded areas, labels, or any combination
  • Works in both standard Datasette and Datasette Lite
  • Interactive annotation editing in the chart builder UI

🧪 How It Works

A chart with annotations looks like this:

Same chart in Datasette Lite lets you tweak annotations using the chart builder UI.

🤖 Agent Integration

If you also install Datasette Agent the agent can build annotated charts for you. Here’s what I got on the agent.datasette.io demo for this prompt: ‘Show a chart comparing Simon’s tagged content about LLMs with his tagged content about Datasette, with annotations’

🚀 Availability

The feature is now available in datasette-charts. Datasette Agent support requires the additional plugin installation for automated chart generation.

#Datasette #data-visualization #annotations #charts

item.title: Datasette Agent Gains Charting Integration
item.description:
Datasette Agent Gains Charting Integration

Datasette Agent has gained integration with a new charting plugin for Datasette. This allows users to request charts through chat, with the agent generating them using the same underlying chart suggestion and generation tools.

🧩 How it works

  • Users can ask the chat interface to create a chart.
  • The system utilizes the same underlying chart suggestion and generation tools used by the standalone plugin.
  • This integration was part of the datasette-charts 0.2a0 release.

⚙️ Key details

  • A related improvement to Datasette Agent allows chat sessions to open an iframe side panel.
  • This panel can navigate to different pages.
  • The version improves navigation by fragment hashes.
  • This feature enables deeper integration with other Datasette plugins that update fragment hashes when users interact with the plugin in ways that change state.

🚀 Availability

  • A demo video is available showing the integration on agent.datasette.io.
  • Users can sign in with GitHub to try the plugin themselves.
  • A Markdown export of the chat from the demo video is provided.

#Datasette #Charting #AIAgents #Python #DataVisualization

item.title: New Datasette Charts Plugin Visualizes All Data Rows with AI Assistance
item.description:
New Datasette Charts Plugin Visualizes All Data Rows with AI Assistance

I’ve been thinking about this problem for over a year now, but on Sunday I finally fired up Claude Fable 5.2 to build an initial prototype. The prototype went so well that this is now a full plugin. The new charts plugin works against any table or arbitrary SQL query in Datasette. It defines several different chart types (using vendored D3, Observable Plot, and topojson-client), each with a set of heuristics for identifying when they might be a good match for a specific set of rows. Those suggestion thumbnails at the top are actual visualizations driven by the data, and selecting one pulls up the full chart along with tools for modifying it. You can also manually construct a chart from scratch. As with other Datasette visualization plugins, the current state of your chart is persisted in a #fragment in the URL - so you can bookmark charts or share them with others. The most important feature is that the charts take all rows into account. Previous charting plugins like datasette-vega would only show charts for the current page of results, generally up to 100 rows. The new plugin compiles each chart to a SQL query that aggregates across the entire result set (potentially millions of rows) using GROUP BY, time bucketing, and window functions. Each query returns a result capped at 5,000 rows, suitable for display on the chart. The plugin uses sampling to help suggest charts for larger tables without evaluating the full result set. I’m really happy with this initial release of the plugin. It’s still very much an alpha, but it’s the closest I’ve got to the dream of Datasette helping visualize data with as little required direction from the user as possible.

#Datasette #AI #DataVisualization #SQL #Claude #AlphaRelease

Source: Release: datasette-charts 0.1a0

item.title: Datasette Lite: Browser-Based SQLite Database Explorer
item.description:
Datasette Lite: Browser-Based SQLite Database Explorer

Datasette Lite is a port of the Datasette Python application to run directly in the browser using WebAssembly and Pyodide. It allows users to browse SQLite databases, JSON files, CSV files, or SQL scripts without needing a full web server.

🔍 Overview

  • Datasette Lite enables browsing of SQLite databases, JSON files, CSV files, or SQL scripts directly in the browser.
  • Users can load specific versions of Datasette from PyPI or specific commits, tags, or branches from the Datasette GitHub repository.
  • Over 100 versions of SQLite are available for use with Datasette.
  • Additional Datasette plugins can be installed from PyPI or URLs to wheel files.

🧩 How it works

  • Datasette Lite uses service workers to intercept HTTP requests and serve them from client-side code.
  • Each tab has a unique session ID to ensure that requests are routed to the correct Datasette instance.
  • A web worker runs a dedicated Datasette instance for each session.

⚙️ Key details

  • Datasette Lite can load specific Datasette references, plugins, and SQLite versions.
  • Users can install additional plugins using the ?install= parameter.
  • SQLite databases, JSON files, CSV files, or SQL scripts can be loaded using the &url= parameter.
  • Metadata files can be loaded using the &metadata= parameter.
  • Fragment hashes can be used to navigate to specific locations within Datasette.

🚀 Availability

  • Datasette Lite is available at lite.datasette.io.

💡 Why it matters

  • Datasette Lite is a powerful tool for linking to demos of work-in-progress features or bug reproductions.
  • It simplifies the process of demonstrating and fixing bugs by allowing users to share URLs with specific configurations.
  • Datasette Lite is already being used as part of the Datasette development process.

📊 Example

  • Example URL: https://lite.datasette.io/?install=datasette-maplibre&url=https://simonw.github.io/datasette-maplibre/demo.db&metadata=https://simonw.github.io/datasette-maplibre/metadata.yml#/demo/capitals_and_countries%23map=0/4.2/180&color=continent

#Datasette #SQLite #WebAssembly #Pyodide #BrowserBased

Source: Running the full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers and Pyodide

item.title: Datasette Lite runs full Python web app in browser via WebAssembly
item.description:
Datasette Lite runs full Python web app in browser via WebAssembly

Datasette Lite allows the full server-side Datasette Python web application to run directly inside a user’s browser using WebAssembly and Pyodide.

🧩 How it works

When the demo is launched, the browser downloads and executes a full Python interpreter, installs the datasette package and its dependencies, and starts the application in a Web Worker.

  • Datasette pages are displayed in a full-window <iframe> pointing to URLs under /app/<session>/.
  • A service worker (sw.js) intercepts requests (link clicks, form submissions, fetch calls, static assets) and relays them to the Datasette ASGI application running in Pyodide.
  • This architecture supports Datasette’s own JavaScript, plugin assets, POST forms, CSRF protection, sign-in cookies, and file uploads/downloads.
  • Streaming responses, such as server-sent events or CSV exports, are processed as they are produced.
  • If a client disconnects or aborts a fetch, the Datasette application is notified that the client has disconnected.
  • Cookies are stored in a cookie jar inside the Python ASGI bridge, lasting until the tab is closed or reloaded.

⚙️ Key details

  • Browser Requirements: Requires a browser with service worker support. Private browsing modes that disable service workers are not compatible.
  • Web Worker Support: Requires module workers (Chrome 80, Safari 15, Firefox 114 or later).
  • Python Version: Uses Python 3.14 from Pyodide 314.0.8.
  • Error Handling:
    • 503 returned if the tab has already been closed or reloaded.
    • 504 returned if the tab stops answering partway through a request (after four minutes).
    • 500 returned if the Pyodide worker itself fails.
    • 409 returned if a tab was opened before an incompatible update.
  • Session Management: Each tab receives a random session identifier, allowing multiple instances with different data to run simultaneously.
  • Navigation: The page mirrors the iframe’s location into its fragment to ensure the back button works and URLs are bookmarkable.
  • Security: Links to external sites open in a new window with noopener.

🚀 Availability and Versioning

Datasette Lite uses the most recent Datasette release from PyPI by default, including alpha and beta previews.

  • Stable Release: Append ?ref=stable to the URL.
  • Specific Release: Pass a version number as ?ref=.
  • Preview Release: ?ref=pre is equivalent to leaving ?ref out.
  • Source Code: Other ?ref values are treated as branches, tags, or commits in the simonw/datasette GitHub repository.
    • Example: https://lite.datasette.io/?ref=main runs the latest development code.
    • Short SHAs made up only of digits are read as version numbers; full 40-character SHAs are required for specific commits.
    • ?ref values that look like version numbers are always installed from PyPI.
  • Plugin Installation: ?install= works for plugins, requiring a commit with a pyproject.toml.
  • CORS Handling: GitHub source zip files are downloaded through a Cloudflare Worker to add necessary CORS headers.

#Datasette #WebAssembly #Pyodide #SQLite #Python

Source: simonw/datasette-lite

item.title: Datasette Progresses Toward 1.0 Milestone with CSS View Transitions and Streaming Support
item.description:
Datasette Progresses Toward 1.0 Milestone with CSS View Transitions and Streaming Support

On November 15, 2026, developers shared updates on the progress of the Datasette 1.0 milestone, which is now 53% complete. The latest release includes significant architectural changes, security patches, and user interface enhancements developed with assistance from Claude Fable 5.2.

⚙️ Key details

The release introduces several functional improvements to the platform’s core data handling and display capabilities:

  • Streaming Support: Output renderers, including built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms, now utilize streaming.
  • Plugin API: A new Response.stream() method allows plugins to register as capable of streaming every row in a table in a single operation.
  • JSON Redesign: The row page JSON representation has been redesigned for the 1.0 standard, and JSON data within columns can now be pretty-printed.
  • UI Components: A new <datasette-copy-button> Web Component has been added to provide copy-schema functionality in various locations.

🧩 How it works

A major feature in this release is the implementation of CSS multi-page view transitions, which allow the multi-page application to behave more like a single-page application (SPA).

Component Mechanism
.facet-results Morphs from old position to new position during transition.
.table-wrapper Morphs position if it contains .rows-and-columns.
DatasetteModal.confirm() A new JavaScript utility method for handling confirmations.

These transitions are enabled for users who do not have “prefers-reduced-motion” active. This functionality currently works in Safari and Chrome.

🛡️ Security and Improvements

This update addresses dozens of bugs and includes a specific security fix regarding private stored queries. A GitHub advisory was issued because private stored queries could previously be exposed, revealing the title and SQL of the query, though they could not be executed by unauthorized parties.

General bug fixes were supported by several contributors, including:

  • Zihan Dai
  • Peter Olkhovets
  • Ilya Khalafi
  • Ankita Advitot

🚀 Availability

While currently available for Safari and Chrome users, Firefox support for the new CSS view transitions is expected to arrive on December 8th, 2026, with the release of Firefox 162. These features are no longer feature-flagged in Firefox Nightly.

#Datasette #OpenSource #WebDevelopment

Source: Release: datasette 1.0a43

item.title: New Datasette Geospatial Plugin Built with Claude Fable 5.2 and OpenFreeMap
item.description:
New Datasette Geospatial Plugin Built with Claude Fable 5.2 and OpenFreeMap

On 15th November 2026, a new geospatial plugin for Datasette was released, marking the first such addition in a significant period. The tool integrates the MapLibre GL library with OpenFreeMap, a free vector map server operated by Zsolt Ero.

🔍 Overview

Most of the plugin was developed using a single prompt provided to Claude Fable 5.2. The AI was instructed to analyze the datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson plugins alongside a local demo file to build a new tool that combines their features.

🧩 How it works

The development process resulted in several specific features derived from a prompt to “be creative and think outside the box.”

  • Displays SVG previews of GeoJSON shapes initially.
  • Loads a WebGL preview only when shapes scroll into view.
  • Displays GeoJSON shapes and latitude/longitude points together on the same map.

🚀 Availability

A comprehensive demo page has been released that functions in the latest version of Datasette Lite. This allows users to load the plugin and a demo database directly in a web browser using Pyodide and WebAssembly.

#Datasette #Geospatial #ClaudeAI #OpenFreeMap #MapLibreGL

Source: Release: datasette-maplibre 0.1a0

item.title: Datasette Updates Long-Standing Chart Plugin for Datasette Alpha and Lite Compatibility
item.description:
Datasette Updates Long-Standing Chart Plugin for Datasette Alpha and Lite Compatibility

On 14th November 2026, a new release was issued for Datasette’s longest untouched plugin, which enables chart rendering using Vega-Lite against table data or custom queries. This update marks the first release for the plugin since July 2018.

⚙️ Key details

  • Compatibility: The plugin has been updated to work with the latest Datasette alphas.
  • Cosmetic Tweaks: The release includes visual adjustments to improve the user experience within Datasette Lite.
  • JavaScript Support: Datasette Lite recently gained the capability to execute JavaScript plugins such as this one.

🧩 How it works

The plugin allows users to visualize data stored in Datasette tables or retrieved through custom queries. It utilizes the Vega-Lite framework to render these charts directly within the interface.

🚀 Availability

Because the plugin is now compatible with Datasette Lite, the live demo previously hosted in the project’s README has been updated to link to a new demo running on Datasette Lite.

#Datasette #VegaLite #DataVisualization #OpenSource

Source: Release: datasette-vega 0.7

item.title: Datasette-llm Plugin Update Adds Support for OpenAI-Compatible Endpoints and Local Models
item.description:
Datasette-llm Plugin Update Adds Support for OpenAI-Compatible Endpoints and Local Models

On 14th November 2026, the datasette-llm plugin was updated to include support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints. This release allows Datasette to be configured with Large Language Models (LLMs) hosted on any platform that utilizes the OpenAI pseudo-standard web protocol.

🔍 Overview

datasette-llm serves as an intermediate plugin for Datasette. Its primary function is to support the configuration of LLMs for use with other plugins within the Datasette ecosystem.

⚙️ Key details

This release enables the use of various local and remote model hosting solutions:

  • Supports any endpoint talking the OpenAI pseudo-standard web protocol.
  • Compatible with local model runners including LM Studio, Ollama, and llama.cpp.
  • Note that llama.cpp has recently reached version 1.0.0.
  • Datasette can be initiated via uvx to utilize these models.

🧩 How it works

By configuring Datasette to connect to a local model, users can run a local server that hosts a Datasette Agent instance. For example, a user can download a database file like content.db and use uvx to run Datasette powered by a model hosted through LM Studio or Ollama. This setup allows the local model to power the Datasette Agent instance directly.

🚀 Availability

The update to datasette-llm was released on 14th November 2026.

#Datasette #LLM #OpenAI #LocalAI #OpenSource

Source: Release: datasette-llm 0.1a11

item.title: Datasette-Leaflet plugin updates tile request referrer policy
item.description:
Datasette-Leaflet plugin updates tile request referrer policy

On 13th November 2026, an update was released for the datasette-leaflet plugin to ensure compliance with OpenStreetMap’s tile server policy regarding referrer headers.

⚙️ Key details

  • OpenStreetMap requires that requests to their hosted tile server include a referrer header.
  • Previously, Datasette table pages used the Referrer-Policy: no-referrer HTTP header, which caused plugins loading tiles from OpenStreetMap to violate this policy.
  • Datasette-leaflet is a plugin that bundles Leaflet for use by other Datasette plugins.

💡 Why it matters

  • The plugin now explicitly sets the referrer policy on tile requests to strict-origin-when-cross-origin.
  • This update allows the host information to be passed while withholding the full path to the page, satisfying OpenStreetMap requirements.

#Datasette #OpenStreetMap #Leaflet #WebDevelopment #HTTP

Source: Release: datasette-leaflet 0.3

item.title: Datasette Stops Serving Rel Next HTTP Headers to Firefox to Prevent Unnecessary Prefetching
item.description:
Datasette Stops Serving Rel Next HTTP Headers to Firefox to Prevent Unnecessary Prefetching

Datasette issue #3046 proposes no longer serving link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages after discovery that Firefox automatically prefetches the next page of table rows.

🔍 Overview

When reviewing the Firefox network panel, requests to a Datasette table page were found to trigger an HTTP prefetch for the next page of rows in that table. This behavior was caused by Datasette pages serving an HTTP link header formatted as: link: <https://latest.datasette.io/fixtures/compound_three_primary_keys?_next=a%2Cd%2Cv>; rel="next"

⚙️ Key Details

  • Firefox has had an open issue regarding this HTTP prefetching behavior for 24 years.
  • An early comment on that 24-year-old issue links to a 2002 blog post written by the Datasette creator complaining about the feature.
  • The author had forgotten about both writing the blog post and the feature itself.

💡 Why It Matters

Automatic prefetching for next-page table rows creates unnecessary overhead:

  • Only a tiny fraction of visitors click the ’next’ link on a page.
  • The browser ends up fetching unnecessary data.
  • The Datasette server is forced to render an entire page that gets thrown away.

#Datasette #Firefox #HTTPHeaders #WebDevelopment #OpenSource

Source: datasette #3046: Don’t serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages

item.title: Datasette Agent Auto-Detects Default LLM Model
item.description:
Datasette Agent Auto-Detects Default LLM Model

On 31st October 2026, the datasette‑llm plugin received a small user‑experience improvement that lets Datasette Agent automatically pick up the default model used by the underlying LLM.

🔍 Overview

  • The plugin now detects the default LLM model, removing the need for manual model configuration.

⚙️ How it works

  • When launching Datasette Agent, the plugin reads the default model setting from the LLM environment.
  • If a default model is present, the agent starts without the -s plugins.datasette-agent.default_model flag.

🚀 Availability

  • The change is available as of 31 Oct 2026.
  • Example command with the new behavior: 
    1

    uvx --with datasette-agent datasette content.db --internal internal.db

📜 Previous requirement

  • Before the update, users had to specify the model explicitly, e.g.: 
    1

    -s plugins.datasette-agent.default_model gpt-6-astra

💡 Why it matters

  • Reduces setup steps for users.
  • Streamlines the workflow for developers testing Datasette Agent.

#Datasette #LLM #AI #OpenSource #UX

Source: Release: datasette-llm 0.1a9

item.title: Parseable Observability Platform Integrated with Datasette via Codex
item.description:
Parseable Observability Platform Integrated with Datasette via Codex

On 6 October 2026 a new observability platform called Parseable was highlighted on Show HN.

🔍 Overview

  • Parseable is an observability platform with:
    • An open‑source implementation licensed under AGPL, written in Rust, packaged as a single ~180 MB binary.
    • An Enterprise version that adds extra features.
    • A cloud‑hosted option.

🧩 How it works

  • Datasette 1.0a41 added OpenTelemetry support.
  • Using Codex, the author figured out how to run Parseable and feed it traces generated by Datasette.
  • The resulting trace was displayed in the Parseable localhost web application.

⚙️ Key details

  • Open‑source binary: AGPL, Rust, ~180 MB.
  • Enterprise version: includes additional features (unspecified).
  • Cloud option: available as a hosted service.
  • Integration steps:
    • Enable OpenTelemetry in Datasette 1.0a41.
    • Use Codex to determine the commands needed to start Parseable and ingest the traces.
    • View the trace in Parseable’s web UI.

🚀 Availability

  • The open‑source binary and its documentation are publicly available as of 6 October 2026.
  • Enterprise and cloud offerings are announced alongside the open‑source release.

💡 Why it matters

  • The combination shows a practical workflow for connecting a data‑exploration tool (Datasette) with an observability platform (Parseable) using AI assistance (Codex).

#Parseable #Observability #OpenTelemetry #Datasette

Source: TIL: Using Parseable with Datasette for OpenTelemetry traces

item.title: GitHub Login Plugin for agent.datasette.io Receives 1.0 Release
item.description:
GitHub Login Plugin for agent.datasette.io Receives 1.0 Release

The GitHub login plugin used on the agent.datasette.io demo site has received a 1.0 release. The update resolves an issue where authenticated user sessions were expiring prematurely due to missing cookie parameters.

🔍 Overview

While running the GitHub login plugin on the agent.datasette.io demo site, it was observed that authenticated sessions were not lasting very long. Investigation revealed that the plugin was setting cookies without a Max-Age parameter. Consequently, these cookies were expiring at the end of a browser session. This behavior occurs frequently in Mobile Safari, regardless of how the application is being used.

⚙️ Key details

The update includes the following changes and technical details:

  • Session Fix: The cookie expiration issue was resolved in pull request #80 by addressing the missing Max-Age parameter.
  • Compatibility: The plugin has been thoroughly tested against both Datasette 0.65.x and Datasette 1.0ax.
  • Version Bump: Because the plugin has been around for a significant period and is fully tested, it has been officially promoted to a 1.0 release.

#Datasette #GitHubLogin #WebDevelopment #SoftwareRelease

Source: Release: datasette-auth-github 1.0

item.title: Datasette Releases Security Patches Developed with Frontier AI Models
item.description:
Datasette Releases Security Patches Developed with Frontier AI Models

Datasette has released two new security patch versions, 1.0a39 and 0.65.4, following a security audit conducted using frontier AI models.

🚀 Availability

Security fixes are available for the following versions:

  • 1.0a39 (current alpha series)
  • 0.65.4 (stable 0.65.x family)

These patches are recommended for users running Datasette instances on the public web, specifically those mixing public and private tables.

⚙️ Key details

Following issues reported by Sevban Dönmez, Alex Garcia and a collaborator conducted an audit using the following models:

Model Role
Claude Fable 5.1 Security Audit
GPT-5.6 Security Audit
GPT-6 Astra Security Audit

Development of the fixes took place over nearly a week in a shared private repository. For most issues, one person created automated tests to highlight the problem, while the other implemented the fix.

💡 Why it matters

Datasette will be incorporating security audits by frontier models into all of its development work going forward.

#Datasette #Cybersecurity #LLM #SoftwareDevelopment

Source: Datasette 1.0a39 and 0.65.4 security releases
